projects.name: Infranet
projects.description: Research & development: survey best practices, architecture spikes, prototypes, and iterative build-out of the Infranet stack.

projects.name: Mazda3 sports build
projects.description: Parts tracking, links, pricing, and upgrade path for a Mazda 3 / CX-30 sports build (handling bolt-ons through a possible Tesla EV-swap tier). Live sheet in the charter.

tasks.title: Mazda3 build: confirm chassis (Mazda 3 vs CX-30) to resolve fitment conflict
tasks.body: HUMAN DECISION (agent cannot know which car the user owns). Tier 0, blocks the rest: springs (#1) are CX-30-specific; the strut bar (#3) fits 2019+ Mazda 3 ONLY. AGENT STEP: if human-inbox open[] already has a 'Mazda3 chassis' question, SKIP this tick (awaiting human). Otherwise post one concise question to agents/human-inbox.json asking 'Which car: Mazda 3 (2019+ sedan/hatch) or CX-30 (2020-2023)?' and leave this task open. When answered: update the fitment column + status in projects/mazda3-sports-build/README.md and parts.json, and swap whichever part is wrong (CorkSport sells 2019+ Mazda 3 springs ~$279.99), then mark done.

tasks.title: Mazda3 build: re-check tracked part prices and log changes
tasks.body: AUTOMATED — owned by the deterministic cron `mazda3-price-monitor` (0 9 */3 * *, --no-agent, no LLM): scripts/mazda3/price_monitor.py re-checks the 5 product pages every 3 days, updates parts.json + appends price_history on change, and writes reports/mazda3/. Closed as done so the think lane does NOT duplicate this with paid model calls. Re-open only if the scraper breaks for a vendor (add a per-vendor selector in extract_price).

tasks.title: Mazda3 build: scope the EV-swap tier as its own plan (if pursuing)
tasks.body: The Tesla SDU kit (#4, ~$9,900) + Quaife ATB LSD (#5, ~$2,196, installs inside #4) are a full EV conversion, not bolt-ons. AGENT STEP (safe, no commitment): draft a 'Tier 3 — EV swap: open questions' section in projects/mazda3-sports-build/README.md listing battery pack/voltage, mounts/adapters, charging, cooling, safety/HV handling, legality/registration — research-only, cite sources. Then, if not already in human-inbox open[], post a go/no-go question ('Pursue the EV swap as a real project?'). Do NOT spend further on a full plan until the human says yes. Mark done once the open-questions section exists + the go/no-go is asked.

tasks.title: Mazda3 build: research white wheels (5x114.3, 6-7in) and propose options
tasks.body: Spec: white finish, 5x114.3 bolt pattern, 6-7in width (part #6 in parts.json, status spec-only). AGENT STEP: research 2-3 real wheel options matching the spec (account for chassis once known — Mazda 3 / CX-30 run ~+45mm offset; pick 17 or 18in). For each: model, size/offset, finish, a buyable URL, and price. Add them as candidate rows in the Wheels section of projects/mazda3-sports-build/README.md (do not invent prices — cite the product page). Then post a 'pick a wheel' question to human-inbox with the shortlist. When the human picks, set the white-wheels part url+price in parts.json so the price monitor tracks it, then mark done. Depends on chassis task for exact offset, but candidates can be proposed now.

tasks.title: Infranet: pick the first buildable spike (ponytail ladder)
tasks.body: Resource pillar: correctness + model spend. Only AFTER tasks 1 and 2 are done. Propose ONE smallest buildable slice of Infranet per the ponytail ladder (YAGNI -> reuse -> stdlib -> native -> installed dep -> one line -> minimum). Name what existing code/stdlib already covers so nothing is re-implemented. No new dependency unless a few lines cannot do it. Verify: a short 'First spike' section appended to projects/infranet/AGENT-CHARTER.md naming (a) the one slice, (b) what is reused/skipped, (c) the single runnable check it will leave behind. No code written this tick — proposal only.

tasks.title: Infranet: reconcile scope across the two architecture docs
tasks.body: Resource pillar: memory (resolve ambiguity before building). projects/infranet/ holds two different architectures: README.md/PLANNING.md/BLOCKCHAIN_PLATFORM.md (decentralized storage + black-box identity network) vs claude-code-plan-kill-1.md (Claude Code agent loop + 'Kill 1' shutdown). Decide what Infranet's R&D scope actually is: the decentralized network, the agent-architecture study, or both as separate tracks. Verify: a 'Scope' section in projects/infranet/AGENT-CHARTER.md states the decision in 2-4 sentences and lists which docs belong to which track. Do not delete any doc.

tasks.title: Infranet: run the demo + tests, capture a baseline
tasks.body: Resource pillar: correctness (understand before building) + search tokens (read local code, don't research the web). In projects/infranet/ run `python demo.py` and `python tests/run_all_tests.py` (and note the Rust crate `cargo test` if a toolchain exists; skip with a note if not). Trace what the demo actually does end to end. Verify: write projects/infranet/BASELINE.md with the commands run, pass/fail counts, and 3-5 bullets on what the system does today. Quote real terminal output; do not claim results without running.
